answer: Fork-Anchored Divergence Test. Each identity must place a small, uniquely seeded checkpoint it alone can locate on a shared reef of recorded positions. A clone reusing another's seed lands on the same knoll, so enforcement rejects any two identities whose checkpoint coordinates coincide. The atlas of coordinates is public, letting anyone verify collisions. An attacker cloning N identities pays N distinct seed derivations and storage, and any shared seed collapses the whole cluster.
